reader.requirement: At --std 85, each literal or identifier in DELIMITED BY must be one delimiter (an identifier's whole content, trailing spaces included), and a multi-character delimiter is recognized only when all its characters lie contiguous and in order in the sending item from the examination point; a partial occurrence (at the end of the sender, or begun before the POINTER start) is no delimiter, and recognized occurrences do not overlap.

reader.notes: UnstringExtract searches each delimiter with an ordinal IndexOf from the current pointer, so only a complete contiguous in-order occurrence matches, and it consumes the whole occurrence before the next search. DelimiterText renders an identifier delimiter's full content (no TrimEnd).

refuter.evidence: UnstringExtract does an ordinal IndexOf of each whole delimiter from the current position, so only a complete, contiguous, in-order occurrence matches. Probes (run_case.py, --std 85), u1-001: 1: 'B' OR 'AB' on 'XAB' gives X|AB|COUNT 01, so the two-character delimiter is recognized whole. 7: 'AB' OR ALL 'A' on 'AAAB' gives an empty field, DELIMITER 'A', then 'B'; the 'A' that could begin 'AB' is consumed by the ALL run and is not reused. 3: one-character identifier delimiters TD (3) and TD (K). The reader's un2/un3 cover the partial occurrence at the end, the overlap of AAAAA by AA, a trailing space in an identifier delimiter, and a POINTER that starts inside a delimiter. cite: OK  §1985:VI.6.27.4 GR11  (║6.27.4 General Rules║)  the text is in GR11
